A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RAP with the same method and benchmark suite. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original RAP evaluations on NAVSIM v1/v2, Waymo vision-based driving and Bench2Drive, together with rasterization, augmentation and alignment ablations in Section 4.2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds an alignment-direction comparison and qualitative evaluations in Appendix A.1, Table 7 and Figures 7–8.

M1.justification: The rasterization procedure, augmentations, architectures and losses are unchanged. Appendix A.1's Real-to-Raster terminology matches v1 Section 3.3, which already freezes raster features and updates real features; the newly compared directions are experimental alternatives.

E1.justification: The datasets and four benchmark tasks are retained; WOD-E2E is a naming update. Figure 7 adds targeted nuPlan tests involving unannotated signs and LED arrows under real versus rasterized inference inputs, modestly extending explicitly evaluated input conditions.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds Raster-to-Real and symmetric alignment as comparators to the proposed Real-to-Raster direction. Comparator membership in the existing benchmark tables and ablations remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The new direction comparison fixes the real-data fraction at 50% using the Section 4.2 setup. Figure 7 introduces a controlled comparison that holds the trained RAP-DINO model fixed while switching real and rasterized inputs. Existing benchmark splits, metrics and training settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused alignment-direction ablation, two nuPlan case studies testing retention of cues absent from rasterization, and four Waymo qualitative examples. These limited analyses supplement the unchanged rasterization, perturbation, alignment and scaling studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The existing scaling fit is retained, and the new alignment table supplies point estimates without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports MinADE of 1.12 for Raster-to-Real, 1.14 for symmetric alignment and 1.02 for Real-to-Raster at 50% real data. Figures 7–8 add qualitative successes and a raster-input failure. Existing benchmark and ablation results are retained.

T1.justification: The geometric definitions, projection and loss equations, and gradient-reversal schedule are unchanged. The new information-preservation arguments are qualitative explanations, without new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: scalable rasterization, feature alignment and augmented planning, with claimed leading performance on four benchmarks. The appendix additions support these claims without redefining their core scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.1 discusses omitted visual cues and potential alignment information loss, frames rasterization as complementary to real images, and attributes information preservation to multitask supervision. It also proposes adaptive alignment as future work; the original imitation-learning and causal-confusion limitation remains.

D1.justification: A new reproducibility statement promises source code and configuration release with the camera-ready version, without establishing actual availability. Hyperparameters, hardware, Waymo fine-tuning and ensembling, and Bench2Drive preprocessing were already disclosed in v1 and are retained or relocated.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the Ettinger et al. motion-dataset citation with Xu et al.'s WOD-E2E paper and adds Yu et al. on representation alignment to support the new discussion. The broader related-work positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main scientific narrative is largely unchanged. v2 adds Ethics and Reproducibility statements and an appendix discussion, reorders existing appendix sections, and makes limited terminology, wording and publication-header edits.

P2.justification: v2 adds one compact alignment table and two multipanel qualitative figures. The original hyperparameter Table 7 becomes Table 8, and rasterization Figure 7 becomes Figure 9 without substantive display changes. Other changes concern conference headers and appendix layout.

improvement.justification: Table 7 and Figures 7–8 provide useful additional support for the alignment choice and the ability to use cues omitted by rasterization. Appendix A.1 also clarifies the complementary role of real images. The gains are limited: selected cases and one data-ratio comparison do not establish the broad absence of information loss asserted in the discussion. The main method and benchmark evidence remain intact.
